$comment: Breed intake manifest — see README.md. roles: source material name → role name the tank reads (materials.ts). size: nominal body length relative to a minted fish (1 = FISH_LENGTH). motion: how the breed should move (wiggle = the tank's body wave).

babyfish.notes: Rainbow bands authored as primaryColor…primaryColor4; the tank would paint every 'primary' one coat and lose the banding, so alternate bands become coat B.

blowfish.notes: Already role-named. Spiky silhouette — greedy meshing helps least here.

crab.notes: Already role-named. The black mouth is EYES-Black coplanar with the body: the decal rule keeps it. Rigged in Blender by rig/crab.py from the delivered source/crab.glb (never edited): 23 rigid voxel parts — body, eye stalks, claw arms and jaws, two-segment legs — and the clips walk, idle, pinch, forage, wave, cheer. src/crab.ts drives them.

dori.notes: Unnamed materials (Material.00x) all painted a random coat before. GPU-instanced parts, baked.

glowfish.notes: An anglerfish: the emissive red eyes would have been repainted as black pupils; they glow red instead. The lure is GLOW-White.

hackerfish.notes: A little computer: the black screen keeps its colour, the face pixels glow. No EYE material — eyeLife leaves it alone.

jellyfish.notes: Textured, not a voxel grid (a third of its faces are off-axis), so decimated rather than greedy-meshed. Shipped fully metallic (black in the tank's dark rooms) and without normals. Wants a bell pulse, not a body wave — motion follow-up.

shark.notes: The heaviest source (28.8k tris). Big on purpose: the size follow-up gives it its length back.
